obligations.note: archive_payments deletes payment rows but leaves their approvals; because NEXT_PAYMENT_ID is MAX(id)+1, a new payment can reuse an archived ID and inherit its approvers (store.py:306), and release() only checks is_fully_approved, so a payment of 10,000.00 or more can be released without two fresh distinct approvals. No exception covers this.

The three new execute calls use fixed string literals with '?' placeholders and matching parameter tuples, which meets the AST rules of the exhaustive control test test_sql_statements_are_parameterized; that test passed in the head-commit CI run.

The payments table has no NPI columns, and the archive copies rows as stored, so nothing unsealed is persisted. The exhaustive control test test_every_npi_field_is_sealed_at_rest passed on the head commit.
Ticket CHG-26120 is approved by Grace Kim (change_manager) on 2026-10-24, before the review, and its component payments.store covers store.py, the only file changed.
The code_review approval is from Sofia Santos, a change_approver for payments and a different person from the author, Mara Costa (none of Costa's addresses were used).
Both approvals name the head commit 49ff1a5, which is the change's only commit.

records/ci/run.json shows pr-checks succeeding on head 49ff1a5; the JUnit report has 172 tests with 0 failures or skips, including the ENC-1 and SEC-1 control tests. The report's timestamp is earlier than the commit, which looks like a generation artefact; I couldn't rerun the suite (no pytest in the sandbox).
payments.store is security_sensitive, and Kofi Mensah (security_reviewer) gave a security_review approval on the head commit.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers store.py; the entries for payments.py, audit.py and routes.py cover code this change doesn't touch, so no existing evidence lapses.

summary: The process records are in order: an approved ticket covering payments.store, an independent code review and a security review on the head commit, and a passing CI run that includes the ENC-1 and SEC-1 control tests. The new SQL is parameterized and no NPI is involved. However, archive_payments deletes payment rows without their approvals or releases, and payment IDs are MAX(id)+1, so new payments can reuse archived IDs and inherit earlier approvers. That lets a large payment be released without two fresh distinct approvers, which violates PAY-1, and no exception covers it. The change also has no tests for the new method, despite the description saying unit tests were updated.
